item: the scheduler's exclusive hold is counted and each claim is released by the operation that took it, so a window that ends inside a standalone restore no longer releases the restore's hold (R383, OPEN_QUEUE 2026-10-27 item 23)
summary: BEFORE: BackgroundScheduler._exclusive_hold was one boolean. A standalone restore (src/backup/volume_job.py) claims it through the bare pause_for_exclusive_operation, which exclusive_window_open() cannot see; a diagnostics bundle opened inside it claimed it again and its resume released it, so Run now and Start were accepted mid-restore, and a Start the operator pressed during the restore was taken by the bundle's resume and started the loop mid-restore. NOW: hold_exclusive adds one claim and release_exclusive takes one off (floored at zero), answering (hold_ended, start_wanted) in the same locked step, so two operations that end together never strand a deferred start; a release that is not the last queues the start of a loop its operation stopped behind the remaining holder (hand_over_start). A claim is released by the operation that took it: pause_for_exclusive_operation records it in a caller-kept list (claim=, appended inside the scheduler's lock), resume_after_exclusive_operation(claim=) releases exactly those claims, ALWAYS, also inside an open window (where any start is handed to the window), and empties the list, so a repeated resume and a pause that took no claim release nothing. exclusive_window keeps its windows' claims in one set released by the last window out; volume_job passes its claim. status() adds exclusive_holds. tests/test_scheduler_counted_hold.py (11 tests) drives a real BackgroundScheduler: the nested trace both ways (restore ends first, bundle ends first), the two-resumes interleave in both orders, the stray release, a repeated resume. On origin/main the three trace tests fail on behaviour (the bundle's resume released the restore's hold; it started the loop mid-restore); the other new tests fail there at the claim= API, which did not exist. Test doubles of pause/resume in five test files take the new keyword. Stated limits: memstop and the data-drive move pause with no resume by design, so their claim stays for the life of the process; if memstop's shutdown request fails the process lives on with that claim, Start refused, now visible as exclusive_holds in status(). A caller that passes no claim list (none in src/ after this change) keeps the pre-R383 reading: a claim is assumed exactly when no window is open at its resume, so it still leaks its claim if it ends inside a window. Release-notes line: «A diagnostics bundle taken during a restore no longer lets collection restart in the middle of that restore.»
